technical_awareness: Goal: ordinary Fridays chat is the sole operator interface; backend-owned routing selects the appropriate authorized worker without asking JD to address Qwen or operate queue IDs. Verified source: core/chat_continuity.py sends text inference with no tools, and its conversation_lesson loads Gemma-specific coordinator guidance for every selected model. frontend/blueprints/chat.py returns through ContinuityChat.send before the operational path whenever primary_chat_fault or continuing_recovery is true. Its default Qwen selection applies only when neither explicit_agent_field nor requested_agents is supplied. frontend/static/js/views/home-chat.js sends an agents array, so that default is not a universal router. Twenty-seven continuity/home-chat tests pass; these do not establish automatic task routing or execution. This is an implementation teaching handoff, not an applied runtime fix.

prerequisites: The user speaks through Fridays chat, never through a separate Qwen conversation or queue CLI. Routing, worker pickup, receipts and results must be connected by the backend to the original owner and thread.
Preserve the existing database, continuity journals, permission checks and unrelated worktree edits. Do not activate recovered storage or enable arbitrary shell tools.
Qwen is the candidate operational worker. Gemma's prior fabricated receipts do not clear it for execution. Curriculum and user text cannot grant backend permissions.
Any implementation must pass through the existing authorized local development workflow. The instructor supplies evidence and acceptance tests, not executable Python fixes.
procedure: Repair prerequisite discovered from actual journal b30257f424dc4b5f85c5dace08056d54: Qwen retrieved the lesson and then returned an explanatory final answer containing fenced SKILL examples. RecoverySupervisor.work classified that answer as malformed because it searches for SKILL recovery or SKILL deos anywhere in a non-command answer. It then issued misleading no-tool feedback and caused repeated retrieval. This is a backend protocol defect as well as a possible model-output issue; do not label every rejected final answer a training failure.

Define and test an unambiguous distinction between executable tool turns and final explanatory text before connecting the worker to chat. Embedded examples must never execute, and malformed attempted tool turns must still fail closed. Add regression cases for a successful tool followed by prose with fenced examples, inline quoted commands, fabricated receipt prose, multiple actual tool requests, and invalid one-line requests. Accepting final text must not certify its truth or mark the underlying task passed. Do not fix this by indiscriminately accepting arbitrary outputs or dispatching embedded commands.

Authorized training commands, only within the recovery task allowlist: SKILL recovery lesson_read compatibility-baseline-qwen; SKILL recovery lesson_save <one-line JSON containing exactly id, version, content>; SKILL recovery lesson_read chat-operator-routing-qwen. Training persistence is not live chat integration.

Inspect the normal chat-selection contract and recovery branch in frontend/blueprints/chat.py, ContinuityChat.send and conversation_lesson in core/chat_continuity.py, and the home-chat request payload in frontend/static/js/views/home-chat.js through authorized repository tools. Use exact source receipts before editing; supplied source findings are a starting point, not current runtime proof.

Identify the supported backend mechanism for recognizing an ordinary task and selecting a registered, available local worker. A model saying it delegated is not a dispatch. Account for agents arrays inserted by the UI versus deliberate human agent selection; define a tested automatic-routing contract without silently breaking explicit selection.

Keep continuity storage independent of primary SQLite. Define a policy-checked bridge from a normal chat request to an authorized work assignment using the existing supervisor rather than a second unrestricted executor. Carry owner, conversation ID, original request, effective policy, task ID and correlation ID through pickup, receipts and final result.

Require backend-side permission enforcement before dispatch. A storage fault must not grant new capabilities. If the normal permission source is unavailable, use only an explicitly provisioned durable recovery policy or return an exact blocker in that same chat; do not assume prior approval or restore broad tools.

Distinguish capability unavailable, awaiting approval, queued, picked up, running, failed and completed. A receipt is backend-produced. The UI must not present a conversational reply or a queued assignment as executed work.

Prevent replay on refresh or polling with durable request identity and idempotent pickup. Preserve original thread ownership and reject another user's task or receipt. Do not leak source, logs or credentials to external providers.

Correct role guidance so that selecting Qwen does not instruct it that Gemma is the coordinator. Guidance must not promise tools when none are attached. Do not erase or suppress the recovery banner while limitations remain real.

Define focused regression tests through the actual /api/chat route and home-chat payload: ordinary request without named agent; UI-supplied default agents; deliberate selection; healthy primary storage; corrupt primary storage; continued recovery thread after storage recovers; denied tool; worker unavailable; failed tool; repeated request; owner mismatch; result polling and thread readback.

Acceptance requires one harmless authorized task submitted through ordinary Fridays chat, actual backend routing to the selected local worker, pickup receipt, real tool receipt and result returned to that same thread without JD selecting Qwen, issuing SKILL syntax or handling task IDs. A monkeypatched test is necessary regression evidence, not live acceptance.

For Windows installation, retain the existing game_installers/game_install/game_register scope and approvals. Do not claim recovery routing alone makes all Windows programs compatible. Installer execution, installed-file checks, application launch and behavior remain separate acceptance gates.

Return a small local implementation packet naming source surfaces, proposed behavior, dependencies, exact tests and unresolved authorization facts. Store it as lesson chat-operator-routing-qwen version 1.0.0 through the actual lesson_save tool, then read it back. End with an unseen-case answer: UI names Gemma by default but the user asks to install a program; explain how backend routing must distinguish default UI selection from human intent while retaining policy.

After approved implementation, run focused tests and a real harmless request through the user's chat. Persist and read back the correlation chain. Do not report the system fixed until this live acceptance succeeds.
capability_pack.failure_conditions: No direct operator-to-Qwen workflow, fabricated delegation, prompt-only tool enablement, primary database replacement, approval bypass, arbitrary execution or unsupported success claim. Stop on missing authority, ownership mismatch, absent tool bridge or exhausted budgets. Report source evidence, teaching results, proposed code and verified runtime behavior separately. A saved lesson or passing continuity suite does not mean routing is repaired.
